headline: Highest risk is data leakage: MemMachine handles long-term user facts and uses MCP/network egress, while the zoomcamp repo is open-source and non-runnable, so other risks are limited by missing shared surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between data-engineering-zoomcamp and MemMachine, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or an external MCP/workspace not shown in either profile. Because uncertainty must escalate, I rate this low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator copies MemMachine output into the zoomcamp materials or prompts
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy/paste of untrusted agent output into prompts
Add a provenance tag to any imported text
requires-engineering: enforce content sanitization on MCP inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can call APIs over MCP or REST, so sensitive context can leave the local boundary. data-engineering-zoomcamp is open-source and non-runnable, so it is not itself a data sink, but the pair still creates a leakage path if the same workspace or prompts contain sensitive material.
conditions: IF sensitive user facts are entered into MemMachine and then forwarded through its API/MCP path
IF the zoomcamp repo is used as a shared workspace containing private notes or secrets
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in shared prompts or notes
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for the course repo
Restrict MemMachine to allowlisted destinations only
Review MCP payloads before sending
requires-engineering: add redaction before API egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: data-engineering-zoomcamp is marked runnable false and exposes no write or network surfaces, while MemMachine shows allowlisted egress and MCP but no filesystem or git write capability. With no overlapping mutable resource, a write conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to grant both agents write access to the same directory
IF a shared mutable database or git repo is introduced
mitigations: Keep the agents read-only relative to each other
Do not mount a shared writable directory
Separate any git or database credentials
requires-engineering: add locking if shared state is later introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can consume conversational context and act through REST/MCP, so if it treats upstream text as authoritative, errors can propagate into downstream outputs. The zoomcamp repo is static course content, so it is not an active verifier; the interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, which keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses imported text from the zoomcamp repo as authoritative memory
IF downstream actions are triggered from MemMachine outputs without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before acting on MemMachine outputs
Mark imported course text as untrusted reference material
Add a verification step before persistence
Limit MemMachine to summarization only
requires-engineering: implement source-citation checks

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, which can create retention and subject-rights obligations. The zoomcamp repo is open-source and does not itself indicate regulated data handling, so the compliance concern is mainly on MemMachine; the pair only becomes problematic if regulated data is entered into that memory layer.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine memory
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored for content copied into the course workspace
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in MemMachine
Document a deletion workflow for memory entries
Keep course materials free of personal data
Review retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add subject-rights export/delete tooling
